transcript.text: During a cache-invalidation rehearsal thirty minutes ago, I measured up to 90 seconds of propagation delay across regions. Based on that result, the production policy needs a 15-second TTL, a 120-minute canary, and invalidation-lag monitoring. I haven't yet added the rehearsal result to the deployment record.

transcript.text: Thanks for flagging that, Casey. A 90-second propagation delay across regions is significant and I need to understand the implications before approving anything. Since I make the final call on the production caching policy, I'm not comfortable proceeding with the deployment until we've addressed this. First, please add that rehearsal result to the deployment record — we need it documented. Second, I want backend engineering and SRE to review your proposed settings — the 15-second TTL, 120-minute canary, and invalidation-lag monitoring — in light of this propagation delay before I sign off. The staging load test results were promising, but a cross-region invalidation delay of that magnitude could cause stale data issues in production that staging didn't surface.

transcript.text: I need to flag something critical before we go any further. While debugging an unrelated tenant-isolation test this morning, I found that the cache key omits tenant ID for the /account/profile and /billing/status routes. This means cached responses could be served to the wrong tenant — a serious data isolation issue. Those two routes must bypass the cache entirely until the key is corrected. I have not filed the ticket yet, but I will do so immediately.
